searchText: and it's fixed the problem was besu not liking the tx had a brand new account never used before. If you want to try it out at home, it's fairly easy to assemble with my branch, and run with `--network=puxi` `./bin/besu --data-path=/tmp/foo --network puxi --fast-sync-min-peers=1 --sync-mode=fast --logging trace --rpc-http-enabled --rpc-http-cors-origins='*'` for a complete set Would you like me to continue running a besu node, or anything you'd like to do on puxi, let me know. I am going to stop the work there for a bit. let me explain again the problem I hit You used an account that was never in existence to send from. Usually, you'd expect the account to have received eth before it can send. Besu has a notion of non-existent account, which is a bit weird. Creating an account has to be explicit. oh interesting, so not 3074-specific at all. wouldn't that be a problem with besu on all networks with genesis allocation then though?
